full_judgment:
16. He next contends that failure of examining the material FIR named witness rickshaw puller Md. Abdul Aziz and Ward Commissioner Nazrul Islam Dulal, who carried the victim to the hospital, and other charge sheeted witnesses made the prosecution case shaky and doubtful, and the court may take a presumption about the genuineness of the prosecution case as per the provision of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. 

 "The next and another important aspect of the case as argued by the learned Advocate for the applicants is that, the prosecution has failed to examine material witnesses in the case. The P.W.1 in his first information report mentioned the name of one Sirajuddin, husband of P.W.2 Mosammat Rahima Khatun who knew of the occurrence along with other persons. But said Sirajuddin was not produced nor examined, instead his wife Mosammat Rahima Khatun was examined as P.W.2. We also find from the inquest report which is a part of the paper book that Kabatun Khatun, mother of the victim, identified the dead body but she was also not examined. It may be stated that the appellants alleged to have gone to the house of P.W.1 to take his wife saying that said Kabatun Khatun, their mother, was seriously sick. So, from that point of view said Kabatun was an important and material witness in this case. In the confessional statement the reason for killing has been attributed as the victim has sent her daughter Asma to Kushtia with an unknown man which enraged the appellants to kill the victim. The P.W.2 also deposed that said Asma informed her that Asma's maternal uncles killed her mother. Hence said Asma is also an important and material witness in this case but the prosecution has not examined her. Hamidul Islam, son of the victim, was another vital and material witness in this case in the facts and evidence of the case, but he was also not produced and examined in the case. The P.W.2 also deposed in cross that when Asma gave her the information, Asma's aunt (Khala) Mahrun was also present, but she has not also been produced and examined. The prosecution has not only withheld the aforesaid vital witnesses but have not given any explanation whatsoever for their non-examination. As a result, a presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act most be drawn against the prosecution for non-examination of such material and vital witnesses to corroborate or to testify the prosecution case. The learned Deputy Attorney General has also found himself unable from the facts and circumstances of the case to answer the same." 

 "Evidence of partisan witness when appears natural and not tainted with bias cannot be discarded. Evidence of a solitary witness when found reliable can safely form the basis of conviction. Non-examination of some prosecution witnesses named in the charge sheet when does not cause any prejudice to the accused does not give rise to any presumption adverse to the prosecution case.”
